To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) virtual force based algorithms can be significantly compromised by a few malicious sensors, and (ii) the SecureVF algorithm is able to neutralize these attacks, at the expense, however, of a small additional energy consumption.

1) the virtual force approach is vulnerable to an attack called Opportunistic Attack; 2) the attack is effective even if the attacker compromises a very small number of nodes; 3) the attack can reduce coverage of the area by more than 70%; 4) the SecureVF approach can significantly improve coverage, and can detect and neutralize the above attack; 5) the SecureVF is effective and energy-efficient.

1) the virtual force approach, which is at basis of most deployment algorithms, is not secure, as some simple and effective attacks can significantly hinder its capability of providing a satisfactory coverage; 2) SecureVF is an algorithm based on the virtual force approach that is able to detect and neutralize the above attacks; 3) the performance of SecureVf, in terms of area coverage, is remarkably improved compared to other virtual force based algorithms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the security issues of mobile sensor network deployments.
the following issues.
the design of a novel algorithm that can be used in the context of wireless sensor networks, in order to improve the robustness of mobile sensor deployment algorithms against malicious attacks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the virtual force approach is not suitable for mobile sensor networks.
SecureVF is a very promising approach, and should be taken into account in future work.
, while the use of virtual forces to drive mobile sensors is a good choice in terms of coverage, it is not secure, and the security of the algorithm must be carefully considered.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the virtual force approach is not secure and that SecureVF provides a solution to this issue.
the virtual forces approach is not robust against attacks, but can be made robust with little overhead.
the virtual force approach is not secure against malicious sensors and the SecureVF algorithm is a good solution to this problem.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the virtual force approach has a major security vulnerability, which is the first one pointed out in the literature.
, in order to guarantee a high coverage of the area, the virtual force approach needs to be protected from malicious sensors, and this is the main contribution of our paper.
the virtual force approach can be easily attacked and that the deployment of mobile sensors must be designed with security in mind.
